governance.note: pjm-76 recipe VERBATIM on the rule-19 fix (config.iso_configs.drop_drag_owned_reliability_specs): when the ct_netload_drag owns CT_PEAKER commitment, the temperature reliability floor's CT_PEAKER limbs are dropped so the two do not stack into an all-day floor binding overnight (the pjm-76 D-4 off-window failure: reliability_floor x CT_PEAKER 97-99.7% off-window). Grounded floor removal (CAMPD hot-day CT overnight CF ~0.016 vs 0.38 afternoon; measured 941 MW overnight phantom on hot days), NOT a residual tune. Also fixes the meta.json serialization gap that silently dropped the drag from the legitimacy-diagnostics floor reconstruction, under-counting CT_PEAKER forced energy for every drag keeper (pjm-76's committed D-2 PASS was an artifact). No fitted parameter changed vs pjm-76. See docs/FINDING-pjm-burndown-2026-07.md.
governance.residuals_note: D-4 reliability_floor x CT_PEAKER off-window (the deciding pjm-76 failure) is RESOLVED. With the meta-gap fixed, diagnostics are now accurate and honestly surface two PRE-EXISTING issues the gap had masked (present in pjm-76 too): (1) D-2 ct_netload_drag forces 12.1% of CT_PEAKER in the tight 2024 year (>10% rule-20 peaker budget; 2023 7.6% / 2025 7.9% pass) — a grounded drag exceeding the merchant budget in the tightest year, unresolvable by weakening the drag; (2) D-4 reliability_floor x CT_CHP 70.8% off-window (0.0095 TWh) — the same all-24h flat-floor disease on the non-drag-owned CHP fast-start class, exposed by the CT_PEAKER fix. Both are open root-cause threads, not fit moves. Dispatch vs pjm-76 changes by ~0.12 TWh (the removed overnight CT phantom).
